seo.description: Royal Galapagos' Natural Paradise: a 16-guest, 9-cabin yacht with balcony suites, a teak sundeck and jacuzzi. 4, 5 and 8-day routes, 2026 and 2027 rates.

tagline: Nine cabins in three grades, four with balconies, on a 16-guest yacht.
answer: Natural Paradise is a 34-metre Royal Galapagos yacht built in 2016. She carries 16 guests in 9 cabins: 2 suites, 3 junior suites and 4 standard cabins, with balconies on the four Upper Deck cabins. Nine crew, a cruise director and one bilingual naturalist guide sail with her. She runs 4, 5 and 8-day routes between San Cristobal and Baltra, with three price grades.

overview: Natural Paradise is a 34-metre yacht built in 2016, which Royal Galapagos describes as a modern luxury yacht customised to carry 16 guests. Royal Galapagos is an Ecuadorian company running small yachts in the islands since 2012.

Her nine cabins come in three grades. The two Suites (33 square metres) and two Junior Suites (21 square metres) on the Upper Deck have private balconies; a Junior Suite (29 square metres) and two Standard Cabins (16 square metres) sit on the Main Deck, and two Standard Cabins (17 and 21 square metres) on the Lower Deck. There is a teak sundeck with a jacuzzi, al fresco dining, a barbecue area, a lounge, a bar and an internal staircase.

Week A sails from San Cristobal to Baltra via South Plaza, Rabida, Bartolome, Santiago, the Santa Cruz highlands and Genovesa. Week B returns via North Seymour, western and southern Isabela, Fernandina, Chinese Hat, Floreana and Espanola. A 5-day section and a 4-day Genovesa section are cut from week A.
why: Three price grades on one boat, so a family or group can mix balcony suites and standard cabins and still sail together.
Week B is a broad sweep of the west and south, from Fernandina and Sierra Negra to Floreana and Espanola, and the two weeks join into 15 days.
